problem:
Andrey wants to estimate his running speed. Andrey's friend Max takes note of Andrey's position while he is on the track. Max's observations are given in the table below, where $s(t)$ is the distance covered, measured in meters, $t$ seconds after Andrey started running.

| $t$ | $0$ | $2$ | $4$ | $6$ | $8$ | $10$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $s(t)$ | $0$ | $4$ | $9$ | $15$ | $20$ | $27$ |

Approximate Andrey's speed at the point where $t=6$ seconds using a forward difference approximation.
worked_solution:
We use the forward difference approximation

$$
{s}^{′}(t)≈\frac{s(t+h)-s(t)}{h}
$$

 
at the point $t=6.$ We choose the step size $h$ to be as small as possible, in this case $h=2.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{s}^{′}(6) & ≈\frac{s(6+2)-s(6)}{2} \\  & =\frac{s(8)-s(6)}{2} \\  & =\frac{20-15}{2} \\  & =\frac{5}{2} \\  & =2.5.\end{aligned}
$$

So at $t=6$ Andrey's speed is approximately $2.5\,\text{m/s}.$
